Black Box AI Oversight

A Stanford Research Collaboration on Adaptive Monitoring, Auditing, and Intervention Policies for Black-Box AI Systems.

Stanford University

About the project

Black Box AI Oversight is an interdisciplinary research group effort at Stanford University developing scientific foundations and open-source software for the oversight of agentic AI systems.

Research

Our research combines statistics, machine learning, reinforcement learning, and causal inference to study AI reliability and develop methods to audit, monitor, and intervene in AI systems. We aim to enable safe deployment and align system behavior with user preferences and stated guardrails.

AI evaluation

Assessing the behavior and reliability of AI systems.

Human oversight

Selective human intervention to support safe deployment and alignment with user preferences and institutional requirements.

Responsible deployment

Developing safety contracts for the deployment and use of AI systems.

AI Safety Harness

We are developing open-source software for running AI agents with oversight, guided by the requirements of the people and institutions using them.

Monitor agent activity

Observe an agent’s execution and assess its behavior against requirements set by the user or institution.

Support intervention

Allow execution to continue, redirect the agent, stop an action, or bring in a human reviewer when needed.

Improve with feedback

Use outcomes and review feedback to improve oversight across repeated executions.

We aim to provide reusable software that developers, institutional users, and auditors can use with existing AI systems, without access to model internals.
